# Team-scope Phase 1 inventory

Use `manifest.json` with [Team-scoped data access](../../../../../docs/design/team-scoped-data-access.md). `exactParents` records the intended child and unique parent tuples, variant or optionality, lifecycle and known writer modules. These are design tuples, not a declaration that the legacy schema enforces them. `tables` records the current schema inventory. `lineageOperations` records specific writers, readers, scope keys, input identities and revisions, outputs, historical enforcement, required evidence and disposition. `persistedOutputs` maps each audited column to its exact source writer operations. Each writer identifies its path, enclosing symbol, operation, ordinal within that symbol and a source digest. SQL writers record the target columns and fingerprint the statement. Table renames carry writes to the destination names within the same migration, including across consecutive renames. An `INSERT … SELECT` uses the destination column list, not the source projections. Inserts and conflict updates are separate operations. The gate rejects edited, missing and extra writers, including repeated writes within one symbol. A family row is not proof that all its operations have been classified. `behaviorEvidence: not-run` is not an exemption.

`legacy-allowlist.json` covers only executable product sources under `apps/server/src` and `apps/daemon/src`. Each row contains a path, rule, locator, SHA-256 of the matched source and occurrence count. Static dependency fingerprints include the complete import or re-export clause. The TypeScript compiler parses JavaScript and TypeScript invocations and locates them in their enclosing named functions, methods or variables. Invocation fingerprints include arguments and recognized branch or inline callback context. Credential findings cover direct imports of secret-box, keys and token-auth, and calls resolved to their exported functions or methods, including injected dependencies and aliases. Filesystem findings include descriptor and file-handle byte I/O. Network findings cover recognized socket and HTTP APIs, WebSocket constructors, fetch calls and statically recognized fetch handoffs. SQLite openings and process invocations include statically resolved callers of opener and process wrappers, including across relative imports. The gate records alias targets and bound query source where it can resolve them. The gate rejects unexpected, stale and duplicate allowances. Remove the corresponding row when replacing a legacy path; do not grandfather a moved operation. Cross-cutting listener glue belongs to admission, shared scheduler code to workers, and machine claim and upload entrypoints to runners.

Migration triggers are checked independently against the exact hashes in `triggerDefinitions`. Their historical inventory is not permission to activate them on a scoped database. Operational-script controls are scanned in isolation as source text, with test-local baselines only. The deployment-lease control fingerprints each write statement, including multiline upserts. Tooling, generators, scripts and historical migrations do not appear in the product allowlist.

Legacy controls select operations already classified by the scanner, not path-specific anchors supplied to it. Each control removes an allowance from a copy and asserts that the same gate rejects the operation at the expected path. The relocation control rescans the real product sources with one unchanged invocation moved between two already admitted files. It requires a stale fingerprint at the old location and an unexpected fingerprint with the same hash at the new location. The nested-opener control uses a synthetic adapter and includes same-line calls and calls in a named helper; there is no scoped opener in the legacy product baseline. The direct SQLite control adds a constructor invocation to a copy of an already admitted source without changing its imports. The watchdog control recreates an operation that attributes the deduplication fingerprint to the notification writer alone. This is a static inventory, not a whole-program authority verifier. Dynamic dispatch, arbitrary forwarding, provenance of values passed to a call, filesystem confinement, scope handle and generation validity, unaudited lineage fields and the release cutover remain separate proof obligations. Identical calls with the same statically recognized context are counted rather than tracked by line number.

`id-lookup-team-scope.test.ts` and `team-scope-delivery.test.ts` use two listener contexts over one in-memory database, with separate owners, paired devices, runners and complete task/build and Chief chains. Contradictory links are introduced only in cases that exercise them. An `it.fails` case asserts the scoped result; convert it to a normal test when the corresponding path is scoped. Static controls do not execute the operations they classify and do not establish runtime authorization.

Run the source gate from the repository root:

```sh
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 perl -e 'alarm 300; exec @ARGV' node --test scripts/team-scope-inventory.test.mjs
```
